items.prompt: App errors were 0.3% before the 10:00 release, then 20% after. What's the right first step?
choices: Roll back to the last healthy version
Wait until tomorrow, maybe it drops by itself
items.explanation: The new release made errors jump, so restore the healthy version first so users aren't affected, then fix it later.

items.prompt: Errors have been 9% since 12:40. A release went out at 13:00, and errors stayed at 9%. Roll back?
choices: Yes, every error means a rollback
No, the errors were there before the release and didn't grow
items.explanation: Compare the numbers before and after the release. Rolling back a healthy release only undoes good work.

choices: "Fix shipping KeyError for cities not in the rate table"
items.explanation: A good commit message says what changed and why, so the team can read the history easily.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order when a new release makes errors jump.
steps: Compare error numbers before and after the release
Roll back to the last healthy version
Find the bug, fix it, and add a test
items.explanation: Users are protected first with a rollback; the fix is done calmly and then released gradually.
